newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to import 27,000T sugar from world market.
newsitem.headline: Manila to import 27,000T sugar from world market.

text.p: President Fidel Ramos has authorised the import of about 27,000 tonnes of sugar from the world market to replace its planned export of the same volume to the United States, the presidential palace said on Sunday.
The state agency National Food Authority (NFA) or its assigned agent will be given tariff-free privileges to make the imports, the palace said in a statement.
The statement said the importation would replace the sugar to be sold to the United States under Washington's sugar quota programme and help fill the philippine's domestic needs.
The Philippines is a beneficiary of the sugar quota programme under which the United States buys the commodity from developing countries at premium prices.
Ramos's directive calls for the export of the sugar to the United States before September 30, it said.
This would complete the Philippines' additional sugar quota to the United States for the fourth quarter (July-September) of 1996-97, the statement said.
